preconditions.description: The input is a single integer n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() == 'NO') or (stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(line.strip().isdigit() and 1 <= int(line.strip()) <= n for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: If no valid permutation exists, output is 'NO'. Otherwise, output is 'YES' followed by n distinct integers between 1 and n (inclusive), representing a permutation of [1, 2, ..., n] whose prefix product sequence is a permutation of [0, 1, ..., n-1].

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(stdout.splitlines()[i+1].strip()) <= n for i in range(n)) and len({int(stdout.splitlines()[i+1].strip()) for i in range(n)}) == n if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: If 'YES' is printed, the subsequent n lines form a valid permutation of [1, 2, ..., n] with no duplicates.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() == 'YES') == any(all(0 <= (product := 1) * a_i <= n-1 and (product := product * a_i) not in prefix_products for a_i in permutation) and len({product := product * a_i for a_i in permutation}) == n for permutation in permutations(range(1, n+1)))
postconditions.description: If 'YES' is printed, there exists at least one permutation of [1, 2, ..., n] such that its prefix product sequence is a permutation of [0, 1, ..., n-1]. The prefix product sequence is defined as [1, a1, a1*a2, ..., a1*...*an], and must cover all integers from 0 to n-1 exactly once.
